## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`--json` placed before another flag takes that flag as its path, so `--json --junit x.xml` fails. This blocks the "alongside --junit" use that the PR body describes, and it needs fixing.

## Changes
The pull request adds an optional-path `--json` option to `parse_args` and a `write_reports` helper that writes each parsed report to its destination. It also adds `tests/test_cli.py` with tests for the default and explicit JSON paths and for the required `--junit` path.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — Don't consume a following flag as the --json path — `parse_args(["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"])` sets `json` to `"--junit"`, skips that token, then raises `ValueError("unknown option: x.xml")`. Lines 15–16 take any next argument without the `startswith("--")` check that `--junit` uses at line 7. The comment at line 12 says the default applies "when no path is supplied", but here it doesn't. — Users can't put `--json` with its default path before `--junit`, which is the combined use the PR body describes. — Fix: Take `args[i + 1]` only when it exists and doesn't start with `--`, matching line 7, and add the `["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]` case to `test_json_default_and_explicit_path`.
